subject: Architecture
title: Jakarta: The Sinking Capital
description: A short lesson to help you apply Jakarta: The Sinking Capital.

hook.text: Jakarta is sinking so fast that Indonesia is building an entirely new capital city on a different island.

buildup.text: Parts of North Jakarta have sunk 8 feet in 20 years — faster than almost any other city on Earth.

discovery.text: Illegal groundwater pumping by millions of residents and factories is draining the aquifer beneath the city.

twist.text: Sea walls built to hold back flooding are sinking too — creating a bathtub effect that traps rainwater inside.

climax.text: Nusantara, the new capital in Borneo, is being built from scratch — a planned city for 1.9 million people.

punchline.text: When your capital sinks, you don't fix it. You move the whole government.

quiz.question: Why is Indonesia building a new capital city?
options: Jakarta is too crowded and polluted for government work
Jakarta is sinking so rapidly it will be largely underwater
Earthquakes make Jakarta too dangerous for the government

details.summary: Jakarta is sinking up to 25 centimeters per year in some areas — ten times faster than Venice — due to massive groundwater extraction beneath the city. The crisis is so severe that Indonesia decided to relocate its capital entirely to Nusantara, a new city on Borneo island.
details.whyItMatters: Jakarta represents the most extreme case of subsidence threatening a major city. Its decision to abandon the capital rather than fight the physics demonstrates that some architectural and urban failures become unsolvable.
takeaways: Jakarta sinks up to 25 cm per year from groundwater extraction
It sinks ten times faster than Venice in its worst-hit areas
Indonesia is relocating its capital to escape the crisis

faq.question: Why is Jakarta sinking so fast?
faq.answer: Millions of residents and industries pump groundwater from aquifers beneath the city because piped water is unreliable. Extracting this water causes the clay soil above to compact and sink. The northern coast has dropped over 4 meters in some areas since the 1970s.

faq.question: Will moving the capital save Jakarta?
faq.answer: The capital relocation to Nusantara removes government functions but not Jakarta's 10+ million residents. The city will still need massive investment in flood defenses, piped water infrastructure to stop groundwater extraction, and coastal barriers for the estimated 40% already below sea level.
